records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text are directly supported by the provided page text, covering the purpose of the funding, eligibility criteria, application process, deadlines, and funding amounts.

claims.text: The funding supports capital projects.
The projects help people with disabilities live more independently.
The funding focuses on training, employment, and supported housing.
The funding is especially for young people transitioning from children's to adult services.
The minimum capital cost for a project is £50,000.
The minimum funding shortfall for a project is £25,000.
The usual grant range is £40,000 – £75,000.
Match funding may be required if the project cost is between £50,000 to £80,000.
Projects costing above £80,000 should have at least 25% match funding at Stage 2 application.
The application process has two stages.
Stage 1 applications are submitted via an online system.
Stage 1 applications require a brief project description, total cost, funding shortfall, and proposed timetable.
Stage 1 applications require confirmation of support from the Chief Executive or equivalent.
Stage 1 applications require audited accounts for the past two years.
Stage 2 applications are by invitation only.
At least 25% of capital costs must be raised before submitting a Stage 2 application, unless the project cost is under £80,000.
Necessary planning permission should be in place for Stage 2 applications.
Expert reviewers read Stage 2 applications.
Applicants may have the opportunity to respond to reviewer questions.
Expert panels consider applications and make recommendations to trustees.
Organizations that have previously received a grant must wait five years before applying again for a different project.
Universities and large charities with multiple sites may reapply more frequently after contacting the funder.
Organizations turned down at Stage 1 can submit a new application for a different project at any time.
Organizations turned down at Stage 2 must wait at least one year before submitting a new application for a different project.
The same project is not normally considered twice.
There are two funding rounds each year.
Round 1 Stage 1 applications open on November 20th.
Round 1 Stage 1 application deadline is January 5th.
Round 1 Stage 2 application deadline is March 1st.
Round 1 funding decisions are made in June.
Round 2 Stage 1 applications open on May 14th.
Round 2 Stage 1 application deadline is July 1st.
Round 2 Stage 2 application deadline is September 1st.
Round 2 funding decisions are made in December.
If a deadline falls on a weekend, applications are accepted by 9 am the following Monday.
Projects must be ongoing at the time of a funding decision.
An invitation to Stage 2 remains open for three funding rounds unless otherwise agreed.
The invitation to Stage 2 will specify the latest submission date.
Eligible applicants include registered or exempt charities and local authorities.
If applicable, organizations should have at least a ‘Good’ rating from a regulator like CQC or Ofsted.
Applicants and projects must be located in the UK.
Funding covers new builds, refurbishment, and equipment.
The minimum grant amount is £25,000.

records.justification: The agent's text captures eligibility criteria related to organization type, regulator rating, and geographic location, but omits details about project costs, funding shortfalls, specific areas of interest, and the focus on disability.

claims.text: The funding is for registered or exempt charities (or equivalent) and local authorities.
The organization must have at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted where applicable.
The funding is restricted to the UK.
The funding is for capital projects (new building, refurbishment work or equipment) costing at least £50,000.
The project must have a funding shortfall.
The project must help people to live more independently.
There is particular interest in projects related to training, employment, and supported housing.
There is particular interest in projects related to transitions from children's to adults' services.
There is particular interest in organizations that struggle to raise funds from the public.
The organization must be working with disability.

records.justification: The agent's text accurately reflects the eligibility criteria mentioned in the page text, specifically regarding the types of organizations that can apply and the requirement for a 'Good' rating from a regulator.

claims.text: The opportunity is open to registered or exempt charities (or equivalent).
The opportunity is open to local authorities in the UK.
Eligible organizations must have at least a ‘Good’ rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted, if applicable.
